02

What it costs
to leave it

Three consequences, all of them things you are already paying for whether or not the line item exists.

Everything takes longer than it should

Each new asset becomes a fresh negotiation about what it should look like. Multiply that by everything you make in a year.

Recognition never compounds

Inconsistent output means every impression starts from zero. You pay for reach and get none of the accumulation.

You become the bottleneck

If you are the only person who knows whether something is on-brand, nothing ships while you are busy.

04

How we work it

Four steps, with the real deliverable named at each one. If a step does not produce something you can hold, it is not a step.

Step 01

Define the system

Not a logo — the rules. Colour roles, type scale, spacing, motion, photography direction, voice.

Deliverable — Design system specification

Step 02

Build the core

Identity, marks, typography and palette, tested against the hardest real application rather than a mockup.

Deliverable — Core identity kit

Step 03

Apply it hard

The awkward cases: signage, merch, a spreadsheet, a slide someone makes at 11pm.

Deliverable — Application library

Step 04

Hand it over

Guidelines written for the person who has to use them, plus files organised the way they get searched for.

Deliverable — Brand guidelines + asset library

07

The objections you were about to raise

Often true. The difference is whether the current system has rules worth keeping. We will tell you which one you are looking at before we quote it, and a refresh is a smaller number.

Restraint is a design decision, not an absence of one. Altacrest Capital is in the room precisely because the work is disciplined. Conservative does not mean generic.

If you have someone who can hold a system and enforce it, yes. Most teams have someone who can make assets, which is a different skill. That is worth being honest about before you spend the money.
